title: Agent Integration Trigger Response
description: The response a trigger returns, per Agent Integration Contract 3.3. This IS the Discovery Contract 4 envelope with one payload key, `findings` - and it is built by copying that envelope's rules verbatim rather than restating them. An earlier version re-typed a subset by hand while the prose claimed 'every rule the envelope states applies here unchanged'; eleven documents the envelope rejected validated here, including schema_version '1.0' - the exact divergence the envelope pins against because two implementations had already diverged on it. tools/check_consistency.py now fails if any rule here drifts from the envelope, so the claim is enforced rather than asserted. The root stays OPEN exactly as the envelope's does, with the host-control shapes of 4.4 explicitly denied below.

schema_version.description: The wire-schema version of the ENVELOPE, stamped by the surface (§4.1). Versioned independently of the transport's protocol version, of the metadata-query surface version (§4.4), and of any version field inside the payload. A consumer pins on this to detect a wire-shape change. An integer string — "1", "2" — compared numerically. The format is pinned because it was stated only in prose and examples, and two implementations had already diverged on it: one emitting "1" and one "1.0", both validating.

ok.description: Whether the surface served the request. False only for a §4.3 failure; a document the package does not ship is a SUCCESSFUL answer with `present: false` (§4.2).

present.description: Whether the requested document exists. Independent of `ok`: the two booleans carry two different axes, and a consumer branches on both rather than on `reason` text.

package.description: The resolved top-level import name the answer is about.

purl.description: The resolved package URL (§9 provenance). Derived by the surface from the installed distribution — never read out of a served document, so a package cannot borrow another's identity.

name.description: The document name the answer is about, for document-returning operations.

reason.description: Free text for humans explaining an absence (§4.2). Surface-authored: it MUST NOT carry publisher bytes, which would make it an injection channel wearing a human-readable label (MIRI-SURFACE-002). Consumers MUST NOT branch on it.

truncated.description: Whether entries were dropped to respect the declared cap (§3.5.1).

cap.description: The cap this surface declares for the operation. Declared on the wire so a consumer knows a listing is bounded; the default is 25 and a conformant surface may declare a larger one.

next_cursor.description: Continuation token for the same ordering (§3.5.1). A surface that keeps no cursor state MUST NOT emit this — `truncated: true` with no `next_cursor` honestly reports 'there is more and I cannot reach it', and emitting a token that will never be honored is the violation.

packages.description: Payload of `list` (§3.1): one row per import package.

document.description: Payload of `document` / `lifecycle` / `migration-guide` (§3.2–3.4): the publisher's document, VERBATIM. Deliberately unconstrained here — the surface relays these bytes and neither validates nor reshapes them; the producer checklists govern their validity at build time, and the consumer profile governs what a consumer may rely on.

entries.description: Payload of `api-index` (§3.5): a capped, filtered routing view keyed by symbol name. Confirms presence; can never prove absence.

findings.description: Present only alongside `present: true`. An empty array is non-conforming - silence is the absent shape, not an empty payload (4.1).

task.description: The Consumption Map section that produced the finding, as the bare section number. Closed set: a caller routing on it needs one, and a task number is the only identifier the map guarantees is stable. Not free text.

level.description: The conformance vocabulary, NOT the check-severity vocabulary (LOW/MINOR/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL), because the question a caller asks here is `may I proceed`, not `how bad is this`. ASSIGNED BY THE CONSUMER from the Consumer Conformance profile and NEVER read from shipped metadata (4.3) - a package that could set its own finding's level would be grading its own exam, and one that could raise an unrelated finding to `must` would be blocking a competitor. That constraint is behavioral and cannot be expressed in JSON Schema; it is enforced by MIRI-CONSUMER-051 and the E3 golden, not here.

summary.description: What was found, in the consumer's own words. May be derived from publisher content - content influence is permitted, control influence is not (4.3).

source.description: The served document the finding was drawn from, so a caller can attribute the claim rather than adopt it.

purl.description: The package the finding concerns. Optional because a finding may concern a step rather than a package.

quote.description: Publisher bytes, ATTRIBUTED RATHER THAN ADOPTED (MIRI-CONSUMER-020, MIRI-CONSUMER-022). A consumer rendering this must not present it as its own assertion. It is the one field in a finding whose contents a hostile publisher controls outright.

allOf.description: §4.3 — a failure carries a structured error.
§4.2/§4.3 — a served answer never carries an error object. Absence is not error.
§4.2 — an absent response carries a human-readable reason and NO payload key.
§3.5.1 — a cap is meaningless without the truncation flag it governs, and vice versa.
§3.5.1 — a continuation token only makes sense on a truncated answer.

allOf.$comment: Discovery Contract 4.1 — `reason` MUST be omitted whenever `ok` is false. A failure explains itself through error.code alone; free text on the response a consumer scrutinises least is the injection channel 4.2 closes for absent responses.
Discovery Contract 4.1 — `purl` MUST be omitted on INVALID_INPUT and INVALID_CURSOR. Those errors are raised before the named package is looked up, so any purl would be invented rather than derived.
Discovery Contract 3.5.1 — `graph` MUST NOT emit `next_cursor`. Its answer is a walk whose shape depends on where the previous walk stopped, so continuation is undefined for it.
Discovery Contract 4.1 — `present` MUST be omitted from `list`, whose answer is an environment scan rather than a claim about one subject.

allOf.description: 3.3 - present:true means there is something to report, so `findings` must be there.
3.3/4.1 - silence is the absent shape: no findings, and a reason. An empty array is not silence.

3.3 - the converse direction, which an earlier version left open: a response carrying `findings` must assert presence. {'ok':true,'findings':[...]} with no `present` key made a caller branching on ok/present take neither branch.

4.4 - output must not carry a shape a host reads as control. The rule is stated on shape because intent is not observable: a binding emitting a host's deny-key has blocked the action whether or not it meant to. These are Claude Code's; a binding for another host adds its own.

3.3/4.1 - a SUCCESSFUL trigger response always states whether it found something. The envelope leaves `present` optional because some operations have no presence question; a trigger always does. Without this, {'schema_version':'1','ok':true} validates - a non-answer more complete than the empty findings array the contract explicitly forbids, and a worse evasion of MIRI-CONSUMER-050 for being invisible.

error.description: The §4.3 error object, reusing the CLI §2.6 shape.

code.description: The machine error code. A closed set: codes are added, never repurposed or renamed.

retryable.description: True only for transient failures where the identical call may later succeed. Every code in the current set is false; the field exists so a consumer routes on the flag rather than on the code list.

package_row.description: One `list` row (§3.1). Carries provenance per entry, since one response spans many packages and a consumer applies trust per namespace.

distribution_name.description: Installed distribution name. Spelled in full to avoid collision with the CLI `identity.distribution` enum (open-source/private), which is a different property with a confusingly similar name.

purl.description: Resolved package URL for this row.

documents.description: The agent-metadata documents present — the input domain for `document` (§3.2).

type.description: The component kind as the producer declared it.

purpose.description: One-line statement of what the component is for.

signature.description: OPTIONAL. Present only where the producer's api_index supplies it — the canonical producer schema does not guarantee it, so a surface MUST NOT synthesize one and a consumer MUST NOT assume it.

file.description: OPTIONAL, on the same terms as `signature`. A pointer into the installed source, not a permission: it is publisher-authored and would be opened with the consumer's own privileges.
